title: Age-appropriate SkillsFuture Scheme for Primary to Post-secondary Students from Lower-income Households
what_it_is: Age-appropriate SkillsFuture Scheme for Primary to Post-secondary Students from Lower-income Households

sections.label: Financial support for lower-income students
sections.summary: Financial support is offered to lower-income students so they are not deprived of access to programmes, which is more effective than subsidising a wider marketplace of out-of-school programmes through a SkillsFuture scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: At the same time, we do offer financial support for lower-income students so that they are not deprived of opportunities to access these programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: This is a more effective approach than subsidising access to a wider marketplace of out-of-school programmes through a SkillsFuture scheme.

sections.label: MOE Opportunity Fund grants
sections.summary: MOE provides Opportunity Fund grants to schools to subsidise co-curricular development opportunities for students from low-income households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: MOE also provides Opportunity Fund grants to schools for them to subsidise co-curricular development opportunities for students from low-income households.

sections.label: Student Care Fee Assistance subsidies
sections.summary: After MSF's Student Care Fee Assistance subsidies, lower-income families can pay as little as $5 per month for Student Care Centres in primary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: After the subsidies from the Ministry of Social and Family Development’s Student Care Fee Assistance programme, lower-income families can pay as little as $5 per month for the child to attend the Student Care Centres in our primary schools.

sections.label: Reviewing programmes and partnerships
sections.summary: MOE will continue to review and strengthen its programmes and partnerships to bring affordable learning opportunities to students from low-income families.

sentences.text: MOE will continue to review and strengthen our programmes and partnerships to bring affordable learning opportunities to students from low-income families.

sections.label: Interest groups and fund access
sections.summary: Students are encouraged to approach schools and teachers to explore interest groups, which are accessible to lifelong learners, and access to funds will continue to be opened up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: To his first question, I think we would first encourage students to approach their schools and their teachers to explore possible interest groups to be set up in the school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: And these programmes are not limited to our young students, but also, then, become accessible to lifelong learners across all ages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: And to the second suggestion, I think we will continue to look at how to open up access to funds so that our students can access opportunities both in and outside of the classroom.
